mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen in each of the last three weekly means (-48.9, -45.7, -41.9), so linear continuation of that momentum puts the next four-week mean above the trailing four-week mean of -45.5.
failure_condition: The next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is equal to or below the trailing 28-day mean of -45.5.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS recovered from -24.3 to -7.0 in two weeks, crossing -10; that crossing marks the point at which outdoor activity is no longer fear-suppressed, and the same release of caution lifts discretionary indoor retail within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean rises above -10.0 after being below -20.0 two weeks earlier
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -24.3 at t-2w to -7.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to exceed its t-0w value of -41.9 within 14 days of PARKS first printing above -10.0.

mechanism_narrative: Joint recovery of TRANSIT (-47.9 to -39.7) and WORKPLACES (-50.4 to -44.6) removes the commuting constraint on weekday trips, so retail-and-recreation footfall regains its weekday base and the next four-week mean exceeds the trailing one.
evidence_refs: fact:both series trough at t-2w and rise thereafter
failure_condition: In weeks where TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both rise for two consecutive weeks, the following 28-day RETAIL_REC mean is not above the trailing 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM recovering from -22.9 to -14.4 shows routine errand behavior normalizing; because grocery trips and retail trips share trip chains, that normalization pulls RETAIL_REC up within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises more than 5 points above its four-week minimum of -22.9
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM minimum over the window is -22.9 at t-2w
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM prints above -14.4 while RETAIL_REC remains at or below -41.9 for the following 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL has fallen from +11.4 to +10.0, meaning less time is spent at home; each further decline in the stay-at-home share reallocates trips to out-of-home destinations and lifts RETAIL_REC within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from +11.4 at t-2w to +10.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: In the week after RESIDENTIAL prints below +10.5, RETAIL_REC is not higher than in the preceding week.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS rebounded 17.3 points in two weeks while RETAIL_REC rebounded only 7.0; the parks surge absorbs discretionary leisure spending outdoors, so indoor retail-and-recreation is capped and its next two-week mean falls.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 10 points over two weeks while RETAIL_REC rises less than 8 points over the same two weeks
evidence_refs: fact:from t-2w to t-0w PARKS rose 17.3 points versus 7.0 for RETAIL_REC
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the following 14 days is higher than -41.9 while PARKS remains above -10.0.

mechanism_narrative: All six categories moved together into a trough at t-2w and then recovered together, identifying one common shock rather than category-specific behavior; decay of that shock restores suppressed retail capacity and raises the next four-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact:five of six out-of-home categories hit their minimum at t-2w
failure_condition: A second synchronized trough appears in any out-of-home category and the next 28-day RETAIL_REC mean is not above -45.5.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES has been pinned near -45 for four weeks (-45.0, -50.4, -44.9, -44.6) while RETAIL_REC rebounded; without an office-commuting base, weekday retail footfall cannot be sustained and the rebound stalls within one week.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES weekly mean stays below -44.0 for four consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES range over four weeks is 5.8 points versus 7.0 points for RETAIL_REC
regime_hint: work-from-home regime with WORKPLACES pinned below -40
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC one week after t-0w is greater than or equal to -41.9 while WORKPLACES remains below -44.0.
